Thank you very much, If!

although I haven't yet much time to apply this analysis in real time trading, what I'm finding, from the almost-to-the-pip reactions to a point in price, revealing an intention, to the understanding of some of the price movement I see, yes, absolutely is affecting the way I'm looking at price.

I'm not looking now to a chart scanning it for pinbars or double tops, as I did. Suddenly I found myself looking to a chart and trying to understand what is behind the price, what are their reasons to do what is doing. That is a radical change of perspective. And although I can't understand everything, I'm pleased to look at it and could say, "price has been taken back to the supply zone, because there were left orders to be filled from the original movement. Price is being holding in the supply level making a flag, accumulating as much as possible short orders while there were yet enough buyers to sell them". (I became aware of this change of perspective right now, while I was writing this response and took a look to a chart to see if my way of looking price was changed, and found myself explaining me why was happening what I was seeing)

The people from this community are awesome! Thanks for helping me out with my compression homework. I am having a go at RBD/DBR now. I welcome any feedback.

The first chart is the USD_CAD daily chart. I will try to analyse as thoroughly as possible the PA in the 1H TF. The 1H TF will start from 1 on the daily chart. Hi Gilben,

well done with your RBD/DBR investigation! I was wondering why do you signaling the Decision Points as something different from RBD/DBR. As I understand the DP are, in fact, the points inside the levels where the Decision of price being cheap or expensive has made. So the Decision Points you had marked are also RBD/DBR/RBR/DBD, maybe clearer shown on LTF. If you expand a rectangle from almost all you had circled, you'll see bounces on those points.

Harry

good work up there m8, just keep in mind not all kinks are decision points.. or maybe they are but you will get lost like that because they are too many. maybe instead focus on the ones that broke something like a previous high/low or such. just my thoughts, i could be wrong. and keep up the good work

gilben,

You have a good eye and good analysis. As I tell most people, the first part of analysis is being anal, and your attention to detail is good. I will add on a few observations for you.

Above your first compression zone where the C letter is located you have two areas in blue boxes for buying. Technically correct, but dont loose sight of the higher time frames and where the current time frame is, and in this instance the Euro is winding down and the two buying areas wont have the same effect, they will very get blown through. The major selling areas higher up the chart tell you the story.

Compare the other compression zones and the effect of buyers had on the price when it came back down to test them. Virtually all of them provide little impact.

There are times when price runs off quickly such as prior to your 2nd last compression zone, the 2nd compression zone slowly down price and also setup a move back up to collect more sellers where you see your 2 decision areas way over on the left. This also was a resistance area of significance. Those deep pull backs are probably among the most difficult part of trading, in that they throw you for a loop until you can see where the next most obvious resistance is for a continued down move.

Good work!
